result.rationale: The new refreshOAuthTokens.ts sends a POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with only body params (calcomUserId, appSlug) and no Authorization header, secret, or signature. Anyone knowing the endpoint URL could request token refreshes for arbitrary users. This unauthenticated outbound call is visible directly in the diff and is a real security defect introduced by this change.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, the code `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId: userId.toString(), appSlug }) })` sends no auth header/secret/signature. The diff does not show the implementation of the external `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, so the claim that “anyone who learns the URL can request access tokens” cannot be fully verified from this PR alone; however, the lack of any authentication mechanism in the client request is real and is a concrete security/architecture concern introduced by the change (the code even notes "Customize the payload based on what your endpoint requires" but provides no hook/default for auth).
